name: London Stansted Airport

runway.v: one runway, 3,049 m long and 46 m wide

hours.v: open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
hours.quote: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year

curfew.v: no closure, but government night quota limits apply 23:30-06:00 (movement and noise quota limits)
curfew.quote: Night quota restrictions apply during period 23:30 - 06:00

noise.v: government night quota period 23:30-06:00 kept for October 2025 to October 2028; Stansted limits 5,600 movements in winter and 8,100 in summer
noise.quote: will run for 3 years, from October 2025 – October 2028.

slots.v: fully coordinated airport; every business and general aviation movement needs a slot allocated in advance
slots.quote: Stansted is designated as fully coordinated airport ... each business and general aviation movement requires the prior allocation of a slot.

handling.v: FBOs listed by the airport: Fayair, Harrods Aviation, Inflite Jet Centre, Universal Aviation and Diamond Aviation Hub (XJET)
handling.quote: Fayair ... Harrods Aviation ... Inflite Jet Centre ... Universal Aviation ... Diamond Aviation Hub

notes: UK AIP not readable. Night quota period: the airport and DfT give 23:30-06:00; the ACL scheduling declaration states it as '2330 - 0600 (GMT)', so in summer (BST) the ACL figures would be one hour later in local time - check before quoting summer times. The night quota is a cap on numbers and noise points, not a ban. Handling quote is a list of names taken from the page, not one sentence. Re-researched 2026-10-29: 2026-10-29 run: UK AIP blocked by the session's network proxy (the airport's Pilot and General Information page itself points to the UK AIP for aerodrome data). The new runway fact only adds the designation 04/22 from the airport's Noise Overview page: merge it into the existing runway rule (3,049 m x 46 m from 'stn-facts'), do not replace that rule. The Why Stansted page says only '3,000m+ runway'. The Conditions of Use page could not be opened. Runway designation 04/22 per the airport's Noise Overview page (stn-noise-overview); kept the existing runway rule.
